units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Isaiah 24:19">Targ. Is. XXIV, 19</cite>; a. e.—Part. <he>נָאֵיד</he>, <cite ref="N00656"><he>נָיֵיד</he></cite>; f. <he>נָיְידָא</he>; pl. <he>נַיְידִין</he>, <he>נַיְידֵי</he>; <he>נַיְידָן</he>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on I Kings 14:15">Targ. I Kings XIV, 15</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on I Samuel 1:13">Targ. I Sam. I, 13</cite>.—
<cite ref="Eruvin 46a:2">Erub. 46ᵃ</cite> <he>מיא … מֵינַד ניידי</he> the waters in the cloud are constantly in motion.
<cite ref="Ketubot 15a:4">Keth. 15ᵃ</cite> <he>הני ניידי</he> these (the caravans) are unsteady, opp. <he>קביעי</he> stationary (v. <cite ref="D00131"><he>דדי</he></cite> ch.).
<cite ref="Berakhot 59b:5">Ber. 59ᵇ</cite> <he>והאי דניידי עינייהו</he> and the reason why their eyes are unsteady.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 72a:9">Kidd. 72ᵃ</cite> <he>כי הוה … היינו דובא ניידא</he> when he saw a Persian on horseback, he said, this is a restless bear.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 25b:14">B. Bath. 25ᵇ</cite> <he>הוה ניידא אפדניה</he> his cottage shook; a. e.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 2:11">Targ. Job II, 11</cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Leviticus 26:6">Targ. O. Lev. XXVI, 6</cite> <he>מָנֵיד</he> (Y. <cite ref="M01776"><he>מָנֵיט</he></cite>); a. fr.

senses.gloss: to shake, (with רישא or ברישא) to shake the head; to nod.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Zephaniah 2:15">Targ. Zeph. II, 15</cite>. Targ. II Esth. I, 2.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on II Kings 19:21">Targ. II Kings XIX, 21</cite>; a. e.—
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 95a:4">Snh. 95ᵃ</cite> <he>ומניד ברישיה</he> and shook his head (in derision).
<cite ref="Zevachim 73b:1">Zeb. 73ᵇ</cite> <he>ניכבשינהו דנִינַּיְידוּ</he> Rashi (Ms. M. <he>דניניידן</he>, ed. <he>דניידי</he>; corr. acc.) let us force them to scatter.
